items.title: U.S. strikes Iranian oil tankers for first time in retaliation for Hormuz strikes
items.content: US military struck Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz — the first time tankers were hit as retaliation rather than blockade enforcement. Escalation marker in the US-Iran conflict.

items.title: U.S. strikes Iran as Tehran retaliates, raising risk of wider war
items.content: US Central Command announced strikes around the Strait of Hormuz after IRGC attacks on commercial ships and US military personnel; Iran said it retaliated. Conflict escalation directly threatens Gulf oil shipping lanes.

items.title: Iran claims attacks on Bahrain, Jordan, Iraq after US strikes kill 11
items.content: US strikes on Iranian military sites followed IRGC attempts to attack US troops and commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran retaliated against targets in Bahrain, Jordan and Iraq — regional conflict widening beyond Iran's borders.

items.title: Brent nears $96 after fresh US-Iran strikes; could oil hit $100?
items.content: Brent crude climbed to around $96/barrel on Sept 2 after fresh US-Iran military strikes raised fears of supply disruption through the Strait of Hormuz. Oil is the main transmission channel of the conflict into markets.

items.title: Stocks snap 3-session skid as oil prices, bond yields remain elevated; Nvidia, Dell among top gainers
items.content: US equities rebounded Sept 2 after three losing sessions, led by Nvidia and Dell, but oil prices and Treasury yields stayed elevated — market remains hostage to the inflation-war nexus.

items.title: Stock market news for Sept. 1, 2026: Dow drops 363 points
items.content: Dow fell 363 points (-0.7%), S&P 500 -0.7%, Nasdaq -1.3% on Sept 1 as rising oil prices and bond yields fueled inflation and war worries. Job openings and manufacturing data awaited.

items.title: Hang Seng drops 260 points as US-Iran tensions, rising oil hit sentiment; Shein slides 10%
items.content: Hong Kong stocks opened September weaker — Hang Seng fell ~1.1% as renewed US-Iran tensions pushed oil higher and revived inflation/rate concerns; Shein shares plunged nearly 10%.

items.title: Global Market Today: Asian bonds fall as geopolitical risks lift oil, yields
items.content: Asian bond markets sold off as geopolitical risk lifted oil prices and global yields — a risk-off pulse across Asia driven by the Middle East escalation.

items.title: Hang Seng Index opens lower as tech shares soften
items.content: Hang Seng slipped 48 points (-0.19%) to 25,280 at the Sept 2 open as tech shares softened; turnover HK$8.27bn at open.

items.title: Crude, yields flex muscle, bruising stocks early
items.content: Investors shied from stocks early Sept 2 as yields and oil rose amid inflation and war concerns; awaiting JOLTS job openings and ISM manufacturing data. Dell reported after close.

items.title: South Korea semiconductor exports climb 209% YoY in August, all-time record
items.content: South Korea semiconductor exports rose 209% year-on-year in August — an all-time record — as AI infrastructure demand stayed strong. Counterweight to geopolitics-driven risk-off in tech supply chain.

items.title: Fed's preferred inflation gauge shows core prices rose 3.3% annually in July
items.content: Core PCE +0.2% m/m, +3.3% y/y in July, in line with forecasts; headline PCE held at 3.7% y/y, above the Fed's 2% target. Sticky inflation constrains Fed easing amid the oil shock. (Latest PCE release.)

items.title: US inflation holds at 3.7% in July, above Fed target
items.content: US PCE price index at 3.7% in the 12 months through July, unchanged from June; real consumer spending flat in July, slowing from June's 0.4% gain — stagflation warning signals. (Latest inflation data release.)
